mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes-Benz A-Class 200 CDI engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A replacement engine for an A200 CDI typically costs between £500 and £5,000 depending on the engine code and condition. Used OM640 units start from £500-£1,200, reconditioned from £1,500-£2,800, and fully rebuilt OM651 engines from £2,500-£5,000. Labour for supply & fit adds £400-£800.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a Mercedes-Benz A-Class 200 CDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: On OM651-equipped A200 CDI models (W176, 2012-2018), the most common symptom is a rattling noise from the rear of the engine on cold start. Other signs include loss of power, engine misfires, and the engine management light illuminating. If you hear any unusual sounds, have the timing system inspected immediately - ignoring the rattle can lead to catastrophic engine failure.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Mercedes-Benz A-Class 200 CDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the generation and condition. A W169 A200 CDI is typically worth £1,500-£4,000 - a full engine replacement often exceeds the car's value, making a used engine or targeted repair more economical. A W176 A200 CDI is worth £5,000-£14,000 - a rebuilt OM651 engine (£2,500-£5,000) can be a worthwhile investment if you plan to keep the car.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Mercedes-Benz A-Class 200 CDI engine last?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM640 (W169) and OM651 (W176) engines are known for their durability and can exceed 200,000-250,000 miles with proper maintenance. Regular oil changes (every 10,000 miles) and timely replacement of timing chain components and EGR coolers are key to maximising engine life.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the OM640, OM651.901 and OM651.930 engines in the A200 CDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM640 is Mercedes' own 2.0-litre four-cylinder diesel used in the W169 A200 CDI (2004-2012), producing 140 hp. The OM651.901 is a 1.8-litre diesel used in the early W176 A200 CDI (2012-2014), producing 136 hp with a rear-mounted timing chain. The OM651.930 is a 2.1-litre diesel introduced in the 2014 facelift, also producing 136 hp but with improved emissions and available with 4MATIC all-wheel drive.

mainEntity.name: What causes the Mercedes-Benz A-Class 200 CDI to lose power?

acceptedAnswer.text: Power loss in the A200 CDI can be caused by several issues depending on the engine. On OM651 engines, timing chain stretch can cause cam timing drift, reducing power. On both OM640 and OM651, EGR valve clogging, DPF blockage, or turbocharger actuator failure are common culprits. A diagnostic check with Mercedes STAR or compatible equipment is essential to identify the exact cause.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes-Benz A-Class 200 CDI - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The 200 CDI badge arrived with the second-generation W169 A-Class in 2004 as the range-topping diesel, using Mercedes' own 2.0-litre OM640 engine with 140 hp. It was replaced in 2012 by the W176-generation A200 CDI, which initially used the 1.8-litre OM651 before switching to a 2.1-litre OM651 in 2014. The badge continued into the W177 generation as the A200d, marking the end of the "CDI" naming.

milestones.description: OM640 DE 20 LA (640.941), 2.0L diesel, 140 hp - W169 A200 CDI launch; range-topping diesel with 300 Nm torque
Facelift with revised engine management; power remains 140 hp, emissions improved
OM651 DE 18 (651.901), 1.8L diesel, 136 hp - W176 A200 CDI launch; rear-mounted timing chain design
OM651 DE 22 LA (651.930), 2.1L diesel, 136 hp - W176 A200 CDI switches to 2.1L displacement; available with 4MATIC
W177 generation launches; "200 CDI" badge replaced by "A200d" with OM654 engine

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Mercedes-Benz A-Class 200 CDI is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes-Benz A-Class 200 CDI Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The A200 CDI has been powered by three different diesel engines across its production life - the robust OM640 (W169), the torque-rich OM651.901 (early W176), and the 2.1-litre OM651.930 (late W176). Each has distinct failure patterns. Rebuilt A200 CDI engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: OM651 Timing Chain Tensioner Failure - Why the W176 A200 CDI Rattles on Cold Start
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes-Benz A-Class 200 CDI (OM651.901 and OM651.930, W176, 2012-2018)
problems.rootCause: The OM651 uses a single timing chain located at the rear of the engine near the gearbox. The plastic chain tensioner guides wear prematurely and the hydraulic tensioner can lose pressure, allowing chain stretch and camshaft timing drift.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, tensioner, guides, sprockets
repairOptions.longevity: Best done at first rattle; prevents catastrophic failure

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt OM651 with upgraded timing components
repairOptions.longevity: Required if chain has jumped; bent valves almost certain

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical W176 A200 CDI is worth £5,000-£14,000 depending on condition and mileage. For vehicles under £6,000, a preventative chain replacement (£1,400-£2,200) is usually the better financial decision than a full engine replacement. For higher-value examples, a rebuilt OM651 with warranty (£2,500-£5,000) offers peace of mind. W169 A200 CDI values are typically £1,500-£4,000 - a full engine replacement often exceeds the car's value.
problems.recommendation: If you hear a rattling noise from the rear of the engine on cold starts - especially between 80,000 and 120,000 miles - act immediately. A preventative chain replacement at a specialist saves thousands compared to waiting for failure. Once the chain jumps, piston-to-valve contact is almost certain and engine replacement becomes the only viable option.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt OM651 Mercedes-Benz A-Class 200 CDI engine prices

problems.h4: OM640 & OM651 EGR Cooler Failure - The #1 Diesel Replacement Driver
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes-Benz A-Class 200 CDI (OM640.941, OM651.901 and OM651.930, W169 and W176, 2004-2018)
problems.rootCause: The exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) cooler develops micro-cracks due to thermal cycling between exhaust heat and coolant flow. Coolant leaks into the exhaust, burns off as white smoke, and can eventually hydrolock the engine.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace cracked EGR cooler, flush cooling system, clear fault codes
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught early before coolant loss causes engine damage

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt engine with upgraded EGR cooler and new injector seals
repairOptions.longevity: Required if coolant ingestion has bent a rod or washed out a cylinder

problems.recommendation: White smoke on startup, a "sweet" exhaust smell, and frequent low coolant warnings are early warning signs. Replace the EGR cooler at the first symptom - a £500 specialist repair beats a £2,500 replacement engine. On higher-mileage OM651 engines (120k+), consider replacing the timing chain at the same time as the labour overlaps significantly.
problems.cta: -> Get quotes for OM640 and OM651 engine replacement for your A200 CDI

problems.h4: OM640 Timing Chain & DPF Issues - W169 A200 CDI Ageing Concerns
problems.rootCause: The OM640 is generally robust but timing chain wear becomes a concern at higher mileages. DPF clogging is common on vehicles used predominantly for short urban journeys, and injector seal failure can occur.

repairOptions.longevity: For DPF blockage; try clean first

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete engine with new chain and upgraded components
repairOptions.longevity: Required if chain has jumped or engine is badly worn

problems.recommendation: On a W169 A200 CDI worth £1,500-£4,000, a full engine replacement often exceeds the car's value. A used engine from a breaker (£500-£1,200) plus specialist fitting (£800-£1,500) is the most economical path to keeping the car on the road. For owners who love their A200 CDI, a rebuilt engine with upgraded components offers a fresh start - but compare quotes carefully before committing.
